title: C2383 — SYNC module [APIM] connector guide
introduction:
The accessory protocol interface module, or APIM, handles SYNC's connected-device, voice and media functions. I use this reference as its connection directory: the drawing locates a cavity, and the assignment table explains the circuit recorded there. The touchscreen qualifier matters—a familiar socket address can have a different job in another equipment configuration.

Start with the connector identification table, then find the harness heading and its face drawing. Read the printed cavity labels across the horizontal rows; use the housing outline as a drawing landmark. Next, match the cavity to the assignment table and read across Circuit Number, Color, Gauge, Function and Qualifier together. Keep each audio or video polarity sign attached to its named function. Supply descriptions retain the fuse-or-circuit-breaker alternative.

Choose the applicable with-touchscreen or without-touchscreen row before interpreting a configuration-specific assignment. A blank qualifier supplies no additional equipment restriction; it does not resolve competing entries elsewhere. Shading helps distinguish positions visually, but the assignment row carries the circuit information.

This is a reading reference. Physical viewing direction, housing-release operation, gauge convention and the meanings of Size, Used, the color asterisk and the function suffix D are not defined here. Keep those entries literal. Access, probing, electrical acceptance values and repair instructions require the matching service procedure.

The summary Pin Count disagrees with the numbered positions in the drawing. That discrepancy remains unresolved and does not establish extra physical cavities.

edits.why: I use the printed cavity labels and surrounding housing features to navigate this drawing. The broad projection at the right is a visual landmark; its operating function and the physical viewing direction are not established.

The circuit identifier, function and equipment qualifier explain the assignment together. The microphone, network and satellite-audio entries vary with touchscreen equipment, so matching only a cavity or wire color can lead to the wrong interpretation. Terminal Part Number entries remain reference data; an unavailable entry does not authorize choosing a substitute.

originalAuthorHold: The identification table labels Pin Count as 62, while the supplied illustration labels cavities 1–54. The evidence does not explain whether Pin Count includes assignment variants or represents a conflicting physical count. Clarify its meaning before describing it as the number of physical cavities.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all 83 primary units, five complete pages/one figure and two edits. Original first CLI author covered 54 units/two headings. Complete draft explicitly discloses the count discrepancy and covers all table rows and raw text. Original partial author retained separately; physical count, equipment applicability and literal assignment alternatives remain unresolved for bounded source reading only.
